facts.text: Lakeview is an unincorporated resort community centered on a 50‑acre man‑made Crystal Lake, built from a mid‑19th‑century mill pond enlarged in 1855.
The lake’s clear, dark waters were prized for boating, swimming, and fishing, attracting northern visitors to the Sandhills in the early 1900s.
A 50‑acre public park was reserved along the lakeside in 1903, with planned boulevards and pathways that gave Lakeview its resort feel, though bathhouses have not survived.
Lakeview’s development began in 1903 when Harvey M. Holleman and Percy L. Gardner laid out the community on about 1,000 acres beside the Seaboard Air Line Railway.
After World War II, Lakeview became a year‑round suburb; a nonprofit called Crystal Lake “SUPPORT” Inc. repaired the dam in the 1980s, earning a 2000 National Register listing.
Lakeview sits in the Sandhills, a pine‑dominated landscape that relies on frequent low‑intensity fires; modern fire suppression has increased wildfire risk.
